R076-01.notes: P1 last sentence states a reporter used 'dust bowl' in a news report filed the day after Black Sunday. B (1928 report) is a P3 detail that contained the phrase 'a national menace', not 'dust bowl'; C (Soil Conservation Act) and D (Bennett speech/demonstration) recycle P3-P4 details with no link to the phrase. No defensible distractor. Fact-check: Black Sunday was April 14, 1935; AP reporter Robert Geiger's dispatch of April 15 used 'dust bowl' - accurate. Supporting facts (Bennett/Chapline 1928 'Soil Erosion: A National Menace', SCS created by the April 1935 Soil Conservation Act with Bennett as chief, 1937 Standard State Soil Conservation Districts Law, ~220 million shelterbelt trees 1935-42) are accurate. Saying the phrase named 'the decade' is loose but harmless and not tested. Pure literal-recall item.

R076-02.notes: P1: Earth turns 15 degrees per hour, so 2 h x 15 = 30 degrees. A (15) is the one-hour value; C (2) confuses hours with degrees; D (60) would be 4 hours or a doubling error. Answerable from the passage alone. Fact-check: 360 degrees / 24 h = 15 degrees per hour - correct (mean solar time). Other passage facts (1714 Longitude Act, up to 20,000 pounds, half-degree accuracy; H4 finished 1759; Jamaica trial 1761-62 lost about 5 s over 81 days; 1773 payment after appeal to George III; Harrison died 1776) are accurate. Minor note, not item-relevant: P4 says early clocks were 'largely of wood' then calls H1 a 'heavy brass machine'; H1 was brass with wooden gearing, so this is defensible.

R076-03.notes: P4: a rock Mara had stared at moved and she 'realized it was a crab'; 'After that' she sees the fish, snail, and anemone in that order. A, B, and C are all in the pool but noticed later, and 'After that' makes the sequence unambiguous. The gull comes earlier but is overhead, not in the pool, and is not an option; the seaweed is not an animal. One best answer. A careless reader might pick A (the fish is the first item in the colon list), but the stem's 'first animal Mara notices' points clearly to the crab.
